composition_obligations: T1 does not imply T3: noncollapse must be combined with three-dimensional singularity classification.
T3 does not imply T5: controlled surgery continuation must be combined with the independent width/extinction inequality.
Every topological conclusion is restricted to the source theorem's manifold hypotheses.
object: Perelman's successful three-dimensional Ricci-flow route to the Poincare conjecture
success_lesson: The reusable proposal-level pattern is not 'find a monotone quantity'; it is 'derive a source-specific monotone defect, prove degeneration control, classify bad regions, define a controlled restart, and add a terminal coercive quantity'.

enabling_assumptions: smooth Ricci flow before singular time
closed source manifold for the stated mu theorem
failure_modes: noncompact or surgery intervals require additional justification
a monotone scalar alone does not classify high-curvature geometry
transformation_chain.obstruction: singular rescaling may degenerate without a scale-aware control quantity
transformation_chain.resulting_state: a scale-sensitive monotone quantity whose defect is an integral square and whose collapse consequence can be tested
transformation_chain.transformation: couple Ricci flow to the conjugate heat density and use Perelman's W/mu or reduced-volume monotonicity

enabling_assumptions: curvature bound on the tested ball
failure_modes: no curvature bound means the stated ball test does not apply
noncollapse does not itself identify a neck or permit surgery
transformation_chain.obstruction: bounded-curvature balls can collapse in normalized volume, destroying blow-up compactness
transformation_chain.resulting_state: kappa-noncollapsed singularity models and complete ancient blow-up limits under the theorem's bounds
transformation_chain.transformation: apply entropy/reduced-volume monotonicity to exclude local collapse

failure_modes: without canonical neighborhoods surgery has no exhaustive geometric interface
higher dimensions admit different singular models
transformation_chain.obstruction: arbitrary high-curvature geometry gives no controlled place to cut
transformation_chain.resulting_state: singular regions have controlled neck/cap models at the surgery scale
transformation_chain.transformation: classify high-curvature regions by canonical neighborhoods and locate strong delta-necks in horns

failure_modes: arbitrary deletion or capping can lose topology or estimates
continuation alone does not force finite extinction
transformation_chain.obstruction: the smooth evolution terminates at a singular time
transformation_chain.resulting_state: a global Ricci flow with surgery whose surgery times are discrete on finite intervals
transformation_chain.transformation: cut controlled necks, discard prescribed components, glue standard caps, and restart with pinching preserved

enabling_assumptions: surgery maps preserve the width inequality
failure_modes: aspherical prime factors are outside Theorem 1.1
finite extinction is not a consequence of entropy monotonicity alone
transformation_chain.obstruction: a controlled global surgery flow could persist forever without the desired topological conclusion
transformation_chain.resulting_state: for manifolds with no aspherical prime factors, every such surgery flow becomes extinct in finite time; the homotopy-sphere case yields the Poincare conclusion
transformation_chain.transformation: use the least-area disk width and its surgery-stable differential inequality to force finite extinction
